title: How to edit the slide master in PowerPoint on Mac: step by step for Microsoft 365
metaTitle: How to Edit the Slide Master in PowerPoint on Mac | Lazur
description: Learn how to edit the slide master in PowerPoint on Mac: open View > Slide Master, change layouts and fonts, then close it cleanly.

intro: To edit the slide master in PowerPoint on Mac, open the View tab and click Slide Master. Change the top thumbnail or the layouts beneath it, then click Close Master on the Slide Master tab to return to your slides.
tldr: Use the desktop app. PowerPoint for the web has no master view.
Open View > Slide Master, or press ⌘⌥1, to see the master at the top of the thumbnail pane.
Edit the master for deck-wide rules. Edit a layout for one slide type.
Click Close Master on the Slide Master tab. Press ⌘1 for Normal view.
Save the finished file with File > Save as Template so you can reuse it.

blocks.text: What the slide master controls

The slide master is the template behind every slide in your deck. In master view, the large thumbnail at the top sets the look for the whole deck. Smaller layouts sit beneath it, one for each type of slide, such as a title slide or a content slide. Each layout takes its starting look from the master.

Changes flow downward. Change the master, and the change reaches the layouts that use it. Change a layout, and only the slides built on that layout follow. Edit the master for deck-wide rules, such as fonts, theme colors, and backgrounds. Edit a layout for a single type of slide.
Why masters matter for formatting time

Formatting takes real time. A 2015 GfK study commissioned by Made in Office surveyed 1,017 employees at German companies. The study found that PowerPoint work averages about one hour a day, and that 24 minutes of it, or 40%, goes to formatting. It also found that 70% of presentations used only internally do not follow corporate design.

Treat those numbers as a rough signal, not a benchmark. The survey is from 2015, covers German firms, and was commissioned by a vendor that sells Office automation software. Still, the logic is simple. A master fixes a style once, so you do not repeat the fix on every slide by hand.
Use the desktop app, not the web app

You need the desktop app for master view. PowerPoint for the web does not offer slide master editing. Microsoft's support page on web-based PowerPoint says: 'Outline and Master views are only available in desktop PowerPoint.' If you do not see Slide Master, check which app the file is open in first.

To move a deck to the desktop app, select Editing near the upper-right corner, by your profile picture. Choose Open in Desktop App. Then, in the desktop app, go to the View tab and select Slide Master.
Check your PowerPoint build

Microsoft's Mac release notes show no changes to the View tab, Slide Master, or menus in the September and October 2026 builds. The newest Mac build this guide found is version 16.114.3, dated October 27, 2026. November 2026 updates were not checked for this guide.

To see your own build, open the PowerPoint menu and choose About PowerPoint. If your build is older than the newest one listed, update Office before you troubleshoot. Then compare your menus with the steps in this guide.
Find Slide Master on the View tab

Open the deck, then click View in the ribbon. Click Slide Master. PowerPoint leaves Normal view and shows the master at the top of the thumbnail pane, with layouts beneath it. Stay in this view until your master changes are done.
The keyboard route is ⌘⌥1, which means Command, Option, and 1 pressed together. Microsoft's Mac keyboard shortcut page lists it. If the shortcut does nothing, use the View tab instead.
Some third-party guides say you can Shift+click the Normal view button in the status bar to open Slide Master. Microsoft does not document that. Test it on your own Mac before you rely on it.
Edit the master and its layouts

Here is a worked example. Say your team uses a dark blue title color and one brand font across every deck. Click the master thumbnail, select the title text, and set the font and color there. Then click through a few layouts. The title on each one should now match.
Layouts can break the rule on purpose. A section header might use a darker background, for example. A layout with its own setting may not follow a master change. Check each layout you use most often.

To edit a layout alone, click it in the thumbnail pane beneath the master. Change its placeholders, its spacing, or its background. Only slides built on that layout follow the change. Use this for a title slide, a two-column slide, or a chart slide.
Avoid typing on the slides to change the look. A text box you place on one slide does not change when you edit the master. Fix the master or the layout once, and the slides that use it follow.
Add, delete, and clean up layouts
To add a master, click a spot in the thumbnail pane, then click Insert Slide Master on the Slide Master tab. Read the next two paragraphs before you do.

A Mac thread on Microsoft Q&A from March 2023 shows why. The poster found that a layout read 'this layout is used by 0 slides' on hover. Inserting a master also created a new master somewhere else. Tech support did not resolve it, and a moderator advised against using multiple masters.

blocks.title: Stick to one master
blocks.text: For most decks, one master with several layouts does the job. Extra masters add confusion. This guide found no confirmed Mac fix for assigning different masters to different sections.

To delete a layout, select it in the thumbnail pane, then click Delete on the Slide Master tab. Before you do, check whether any slide uses it. Hover over a layout to see how many slides use it. Mac users have reported that hover text in this view.

If a slide still uses the layout, use Home > Layout to switch that slide to another layout first. Then delete the unused layout. Deleting a layout that a slide needs can make that slide hard to fix later.
Page size, footers, and master settings

Page size and footers also live in master view. On Mac, go to Slide Master > Slide Size > Page Setup to set the page size. Footer text sits under Page Setup > Header/Footer. Set these before you build most of the deck, so the slides fit the page from the start.

Two related guides cover the next steps. See [how to change slide size in PowerPoint on Mac](/how-to/change-slide-size-in-powerpoint) for page size. See [how to add slide numbers in PowerPoint on Mac](/how-to/add-slide-numbers-in-powerpoint) for footers and numbers.
Close master view and return to Normal

When the master is done, click Close Master on the Slide Master tab. Microsoft's Mac steps use that label. Some guides call the button Close Master View, which is the Windows label. Look for whichever name your build shows.
To get back to Normal view with the keyboard, press ⌘1. Microsoft's Mac shortcut page lists ⌘1 for Normal view. It gives no Mac shortcut for closing master view, so use the button for that.

blocks.text: Update existing slides after a master change

A master change does not always appear on slides you already built. A Microsoft Q&A thread, tagged Windows, describes a logo that did not show on existing slides after a master change. The accepted fix there was Home > Reset on each slide.

Microsoft's apply-a-layout page gives the Mac path. In Normal view, go to Home and click Layout, then pick the layout the slide should use. Microsoft labels the Reset instructions as Windows only, so a Reset option may not appear on your Mac.
Work in this order. Reapply the layout to one slide, check the logo and fonts, then do the rest. A quick check on one slide saves you from fixing the whole deck twice.
Save the master as a reusable template
Once the master is right, save the file as a template. Choose File > Save as Template. Enter a name, then click Save. The next time you start a deck, open that template, and the master comes with it.
Keep the master file as a working copy too. A template holds the design, but it does not hold your history of edits. Save a dated copy before a big overhaul of the master.
Mistakes people make with the slide master

items: Typing on one slide to change the look. Fix the master or the layout instead, so the change reaches every slide that uses it.
Deleting a layout before checking which slides use it.
Inserting extra masters when one master with several layouts would do.
Looking for master view in the web app, then deciding the feature is missing.
Skipping the check after a change. Reapply the layout to one slide, then scan the rest.

blocks.text: Where to go next

With the master set, build your slides from the layouts. When you present, [use Presenter View](/how-to/use-presenter-view-in-powerpoint) to see your notes and the next slide. Then scan a few slides to confirm they still match the master.

faq.question: Why is there no Slide Master button on my View tab?
faq.answer: The file is probably open in PowerPoint for the web. Microsoft says Outline and Master views are only available in desktop PowerPoint. Select Editing near the upper-right corner, choose Open in Desktop App, then go to View > Slide Master. If the button is still missing, compare your build with Microsoft's Mac release notes.

faq.question: What is the keyboard shortcut for Slide Master on Mac?
faq.answer: Press ⌘⌥1, which means Command, Option, and 1 pressed together. Microsoft's Mac keyboard shortcut page lists it. The same page lists ⌘1 for Normal view, and it gives no shortcut for closing master view.

faq.question: Is the button called Close Master or Close Master View?
faq.answer: Microsoft's Mac steps call it Close Master on the Slide Master tab. Indezine's Mac guide places Close Master View in the Close group. The two sources conflict, so use whichever name your build shows.

faq.question: Can I edit the slide master in PowerPoint for the web?
faq.answer: No. Microsoft says master editing is only in desktop PowerPoint. Open the file in the desktop app with Editing, then Open in Desktop App, and make your master changes there.

faq.question: Can different sections of one deck use different masters?
faq.answer: This guide found no confirmed Mac fix for that. A Microsoft Q&A thread from March 2023 describes strange behavior after inserting a master, and a moderator advised against using multiple masters. Keep one master unless you have a specific reason not to.

faq.question: Do master changes update slides I already made?
faq.answer: Usually, for slides that use the changed layout, but not always. A Microsoft Q&A thread describes a logo that did not show on existing slides. On a Mac, reapply the layout with Home > Layout, then check the slide.

faq.question: Which PowerPoint for Mac version is current?
faq.answer: The newest Mac build this guide found is 16.114.3, dated October 27, 2026. November 2026 updates were not checked. To see your own version, open PowerPoint > About PowerPoint.

faq.question: How reliable is the 40% formatting figure?
faq.answer: Use it as a rough signal only. It comes from a 2015 survey of 1,017 employees at German companies, commissioned by a vendor that sells Office automation software. It is old, so it is not a current benchmark.

task: Edit the slide master in PowerPoint on Mac
appliesTo: Microsoft 365 for Mac, desktop PowerPoint, build 16.114 and later
requirements: PowerPoint for Mac desktop app with a Microsoft 365 subscription
The deck open in the desktop app, not in the browser
Permission to change the master if the template belongs to a team

steps.name: Open the deck in the desktop app
steps.text: Open your file in PowerPoint for Mac, not in a browser. If it opened in the web app, select Editing near the upper-right corner, by your profile picture, then choose Open in Desktop App. Master view only works in the desktop app.
steps.tip: The web app has no Slide Master option, so this step saves you a dead end.

steps.name: Open the View tab
steps.text: Click View in the ribbon at the top of PowerPoint. The View tab holds the views for your deck, including Normal and Slide Master.

steps.name: Click Slide Master
steps.text: Click Slide Master. PowerPoint switches to master view. The large thumbnail at the top is the master, and the layouts sit beneath it.
steps.tip: The shortcut is Command, Option, and 1 pressed together. Microsoft lists it on its Mac keyboard shortcut page.

steps.name: Read the thumbnail pane
steps.text: Look at the thumbnail pane on the left. The master is at the top, and each layout appears below it. Click a layout to edit only that slide type. Click the master to change the rules for every layout that inherits from it.

steps.name: Change the master styles
steps.text: Select the title, body text, or background on the master thumbnail, then change its font, size, or color. Changes on the master carry down to layouts that inherit them. Check a few layouts afterward.

steps.name: Edit or delete a layout
steps.text: To edit a layout, select it and change its placeholders. To delete one, check first that no slide needs it. Then select the layout and click Delete on the Slide Master tab.
steps.tip: Hover over a layout to see how many slides use it. Mac users have reported that hover text in this view.

steps.name: Set page size and footers
steps.text: Use Slide Master > Slide Size > Page Setup to change the page size. Footer text is under Page Setup > Header/Footer. Set these before you build most of the deck.

steps.name: Close master view
steps.text: Click Close Master on the Slide Master tab. You return to Normal view. Some guides call this button Close Master View, so look for the matching label in your build.
steps.tip: ⌘1 returns to Normal view. Microsoft gives no keyboard shortcut for closing master view itself.

steps.name: Reapply layouts on existing slides
steps.text: In Normal view, select a slide that did not pick up the change. Go to Home > Layout and choose the layout it should use. Check the logo and fonts on that slide before you move on.

steps.name: Save the master as a template
steps.text: Choose File > Save as Template. Enter a name for the template, then click Save. Start future decks from this file.

troubleshooting.problem: The View tab has no Slide Master button
troubleshooting.fix: Check whether the file is open in the web app. Use Editing > Open in Desktop App, then View > Slide Master. If it is still missing, compare your build with the newest version in Microsoft's Mac release notes.

troubleshooting.problem: A logo or style change does not show on existing slides
troubleshooting.fix: Select the slide in Normal view, then go to Home > Layout and reapply the layout it should use. Microsoft labels Reset as Windows only, so do not count on a Reset option on your Mac.

troubleshooting.problem: Inserting a master created a new master somewhere else
troubleshooting.fix: Find the new master in the thumbnail pane and check whether it holds anything you need. Keep one master with several layouts. A moderator in a 2023 Microsoft Q&A thread advised against multiple masters.

troubleshooting.problem: A layout says it is used by 0 slides
troubleshooting.fix: Treat that hover text as a hint, not a guarantee. Check the slides by eye, then delete the layout on the Slide Master tab only when no slide needs it.

troubleshooting.problem: Close Master is not where you expect
troubleshooting.fix: Look on the Slide Master tab. Microsoft's Mac steps say Close Master, and some guides say Close Master View. Use the button with whichever label your build shows.
